newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Quake jolts NZ South Island, 5.2 on Richter.
newsitem.headline: Quake jolts NZ South Island, 5.2 on Richter.

text.p: An earthquake measuring 5.2 on the Richter scale was recorded off the east coast of New Zealand's South Island on Thursday, the Institute of Geological and Nuclear Sciences said.

The institute said the quake was centred 100 km (60 miles) east of Kaikoura, a coastal town popular with tourists for its whale-watching, and was felt as far away as Wellington in the lower North Island.
A Kaikoura police officer said he had not noticed the tremor and had received no damage reports.

New Zealand, part of a belt of earthquake activity around the Pacific Rim, is prone to frequent shocks. A quake measuring six or higher on the Richter scale occurs on average about once a year.
